Key audit matter:
Impairment of investments in subsidiaries
and the HFDI Property Fund
As described in Note 20 and Note 23 of the financial
statements, the Group evaluates its investments
in subsidiaries and the HFDI Property Fund for
impairment annually and records an impairment loss
when the carrying amount exceeds the recoverable
amount. The assessment of the recoverable amounts
is judgmental and requires estimation and the use
of subjective assumptions.
The Group measures the recoverable amount using
projected discounted cash flows.
The key assumptions include projected cash
flows from property sales and the timing of these
cashflows, and the discount rate applied in the
model. Changes in these assumptions could result
in material variations in the recoverable amount.
How our audit addressed the key audit ma:
We evaluated the appropriateness of the methodology
for identifying impairment of the investments and the use
of the discounted cashflows approach in computing the
recoverable amounts.
We performed inquiries of management about the
current market conditions and assessed the projections
for evidence of management bias.
We tested the reasonableness of the property sales
values by comparing with the independent valuation
reports and past property sales experience.
We assessed the reasonableness of the timing of the
projected cashflows and the discount rate applied in
the projected cashflow.
We tested the mathematical accuracy of
the computations.
We evaluated the adequacy and consistency of
disclosures in the financial statements.
